title: Second-layer blind review of T30-R1 DBinder raw-pointer lifetime candidate

scope.method: Read-only synthesis and counterexample audit of immutable raw-source bindings recorded by D29, T30, T33, D41 and T42.

candidate.claim_under_review: After a DBinder worker passes its caller tuple gate and QueryStubByIndex returns a raw IPCObjectStub pointer, a shutdown callback on a distinct TLS-selected invoker may drop the socket relation's last strong reference before/during SendRequest; per-invoker objectMutex_ and index erase may not protect the already copied pointer.
candidate.risk_assessment: Low-confidence conditional memory-lifetime risk. The source supports a structurally plausible raw-pointer window and a possible last-ref path, but does not establish concurrent product scheduling, a last-reference instance, post-destruction access, attacker-controlled triggering, or material impact. Do not label this a confirmed UAF.

source_binding.binding_basis: Immutable target-commit raw-file SHA-256 and Git blob IDs independently recorded in T30/T33; D41/T42 hashes match the relevant source set.

evidence.finding: The function locks this invoker's objectMutex_, stores QueryStubByIndex(cookie) as auto* and calls SendRequest through that raw pointer. No temporary sptr or explicit IncStrongRef occurs between lookup and call. The lock remains held for the call.

evidence.location: QueryStubByIndex lines 994-1009 and EraseStubIndex lines 1044-1057 per T33
evidence.finding: The shared map lock protects lookup only and is released before returning. EraseStubIndex prevents later lookup but does not revoke a copied pointer.
Socket relations are detached and associated stub references are decremented on close.

source_binding_and_local_mechanism.qualification: This proves a source-level lifetime window conditional on concurrent execution and a final reference decrement; it does not prove a use-after-free occurs.

supported_facts: ProcessTransaction calls CheckAndSetCallerInfo before TargetStubSendRequest; the caller tuple is derived from active DBinder session state and checked against server-maintained app-auth mapping plus cookie/stubIndex and socket relation (D29/T30 immutable source review).
The candidate is therefore not an unauthenticated arbitrary local call path; it concerns a request on an established/authorized DBinder session.
unknowns: Whether an untrusted ordinary application can establish or control the relevant peer session in the target product.
Whether that authorized peer can cause the exact request/close sequence, and whether session shutdown is attacker-triggerable rather than ordinary lifecycle behavior.

supported_facts: IPCThreadSkeleton is held in pthread TLS; objectMutex_ is a non-static per-invoker member. Distinct worker and callback threads can therefore have distinct locks (T30/T33/T42).
ServerOnShutdown obtains the invoker through the current callback thread's skeleton; request handling uses the worker path (T33/T42).
active_counterexamples: If SoftBus invokes ServerOnShutdown on the same TLS thread that processes the transaction, both paths may use the same invoker/mutex and serialize.
Even on distinct threads, the transaction may finish SendRequest before close, or close may complete before lookup; those schedules do not produce the claimed window.
thread_scheduling_and_locking.missing_evidence: No target-paired SoftBus callback-thread provenance, happens-before guarantee, or runtime overlap evidence is recorded. Source callbacks alone do not establish scheduling.

supported_facts: Session relation creation increments a strong reference; socket close decrements once per removed socket-bound relation (T33/T42).
If that decrement is the final strong reference, final-release cleanup erases the stub index (T33/T42).
active_counterexamples: A caller-held sptr, service-owned sptr, another live session relation, or any unrelated strong owner prevents this close from being the last release.
The source audit does not enumerate the strong-reference distribution for a concrete service stub at the proposed overlap point.
last_strong_reference.missing_evidence: Target runtime/refcount instrumentation proving this socket relation is the only strong reference at the scheduled close.

supported_facts: A copied raw pointer is not made safe by later map erase; the index lock does not pin object lifetime (T33/T42).

T33 notes the source comment warns not to use the stub after SendRequest because DBINDER_DECREFS can itself destroy it; this supports lifecycle sensitivity but is not evidence of a concurrent invalid access.
active_counterexamples: Close-before-lookup erases the index first; QueryStubByIndex returns null and SendRequest is skipped.
A surviving strong owner prevents destruction.
Destruction may occur only after SendRequest returns, or execution may not touch invalid object state after a destructor marker.
post_destruction_access.missing_evidence: A controlled target-paired runtime showing destructor/OnLastStrongRef before the worker's subsequent SendRequest access, with sanitizer or safe instrumentation evidence. Refcount zero or index erase alone is not enough.

attacker_control_and_security_impact.source_level_effect_if_proven: A genuine post-destruction virtual/member access could cause a service crash or memory-safety violation; the current evidence does not show that access or any corruption primitive.
unknowns: Whether a remote peer can reliably trigger the shutdown/request overlap.
Whether a crash, corruption, cross-principal effect, or only benign teardown results.
Whether the affected stub is privileged or whether the effect is isolated to the session/service.
attacker_control_and_security_impact.conclusion: No attacker-controlled exploitable effect is established. Do not assert UAF, DoS, or privilege impact from source possibility alone.

target_product_and_softbus_pairing.evidence: D27/T28 and D41 report no immutable product lock pairing IPC bbb92dbb2f52aca54ab268307c9476ac1802f3ff with a SoftBus revision. Frozen manifest snapshots pair older IPC 5903fd5f7332a427cb3f6915b0202ee5c76c63b5 with other SoftBus commits; active manifest floats revisions.
target_product_and_softbus_pairing.qualification: This refutes the claim that the current record proves a target product deployment/pairing; it does not refute that some product may use the source.

evidence: T42 inventory: IPCObjectStub handler tests cover branches, close-handler unit/fuzz tests exercise shutdown in isolation, and ProcessSkeleton attach/detach fuzz tests do not coordinate a gated transaction with close.
No identified test pauses after non-null raw QueryStubByIndex and before SendRequest while a distinct callback-thread invoker closes the same socket relation.
existing_test_coverage.qualification: This is an inventory-based gap report, not a fresh exhaustive test search or test execution. No tests/PoC were run for this review.

go_no_go.vulnerability_claim: NO-GO: do not report or promote T30-R1 as a confirmed UAF/vulnerability.
go_no_go.production_fix: NO-GO: do not change production ownership/locking based only on this source-level possibility.
go_no_go.evidence_gathering: GO only when a target-paired product build/runtime becomes available; implement a test-only seam and run the bounded oracle below before deciding whether a fix is warranted.

required_product_material: Immutable product manifest/build lock pairing exact IPC, SoftBus and c_utils commits.
Matching OHOS compiler, sysroot, generated args.gn/build.ninja and resolved IPC test target.
SoftBus callback implementation or runtime evidence identifying shutdown callback thread and proving possible overlap with the request worker.

minimum_deterministic_oracle.test_only_seam: Barrier immediately after non-null QueryStubByIndex returns and before SendRequest; do not hold the stub map lock at the seam.
candidate_schedule: Drive the real request through CheckAndSetCallerInfo and pause the worker at the seam.
Prove by instrumentation that the socket relation is the only strong reference, then use a distinct TLS invoker thread to close the same socket and wait for final release/destructor/index erase.
Release the worker and observe whether SendRequest begins/accesses object state after destruction using a target sanitizer or safe instrumentation.
required_controls: Close-before-lookup: lookup returns null and SendRequest is not entered.
Unrelated strong owner: close does not destroy the object during the request window.
Same-thread callback or serialized request-before-close: no concurrent destruction during SendRequest.
No destruction marker or no post-destruction access: retain insufficient; do not treat refcount zero/index erase alone as confirmation.

minimum_proof_requirements.go_criteria: Only if paired product evidence establishes a distinct-thread overlap, the socket relation is the last strong ref, and controlled instrumentation shows a subsequent SendRequest access after destruction may this advance to a test-confirmed memory-safety defect and then a minimal fix proposal.

review_limits: No tests or PoCs run; no product code changed.
Assessment is bounded to immutable source bindings recorded in the cited D29/T30/T33/D41/T42 artifacts; no inference about unpaired SoftBus internals is made.
No complete inventory of all application/service sptr owners is available from the reviewed source slices.
